correctness.rationale: For an exact two-level spectrum the Rayleigh quotient is a constant plus a positive multiple of the squared overlap with the top eigendirection, so the optimizer over the sampled augmented subspace is the normalized projection of that direction. An orthogonal decomposition proves that the ratio of successive spectral gaps equals one minus the squared length of a Haar tangent-subspace projection. The Haar tangent-plane projection has the stated beta law; its conditional distribution is constant given every past state, which proves independence. Gamma beta moments, the strong law for integrable log increments, strict block merging and the beta/chi-square asymptotics prove all parts of the final claim. The saved verifier passed 837 seeded algebraic/numerical checks; finite testing is not used to prove an infinite statement. Excludes degenerate initial overlaps, noisy operators and inexact subproblems.

value.rationale: This supplies a complete distributional test case for an adjoint-free spectral optimization method under the natural rank-one spike model: exact errors and confidence-relevant moments at every step, a sample-path rate, and the sharp tradeoff between one larger tangent search and a partition of the same number of forward evaluations. With a near-full tangent budget, the expected remaining gap improves from order one under sequential one-direction searches to order inverse dimension under the full block, so the comparison has tangible quantitative significance. The algorithmic input metric excludes the larger Rayleigh–Ritz eigensolve and storage overhead; this does not assert wall-clock superiority or results for arbitrary spectra.
